questions.enonce_markdown:
State the main difference between:

(i) A Server and a Client in a Client-Server network. (2 marks)

(ii) Synchronous and asynchronous data transmission. (2 marks)

(iii) Parallel and serial data transmission. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Server and client (2 marks).** A **server** is a powerful computer that *provides* services and resources (files, printing, e-mail, web pages) to the other computers and waits for their requests. A **client** is a computer (or other device) that *requests and uses* those services from the server.

**(ii) Synchronous and asynchronous transmission (2 marks).** In **synchronous** transmission the data is sent as a continuous stream of blocks (frames) and the sender and the receiver are kept in step by a common clock signal, with no start or stop bits for each character. In **asynchronous** transmission the data is sent one character (byte) at a time, each character framed by a start bit and a stop bit, with no common clock and with gaps of any length between characters.

**(iii) Parallel and serial transmission (2 marks).** In **parallel** transmission several bits (for example the 8 bits of a byte) are sent at the same time, each on its own wire; it is fast but only suitable for short distances. In **serial** transmission the bits are sent one after another along a single wire or channel; it is slower for the same clock rate but cheaper and suitable for long distances.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the main role of the following networking devices:

(i) Repeater. (2 marks)

(ii) Bridge. (2 marks)

(iii) Router. (2 marks)

(iv) Modem. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Repeater (2 marks).** It receives a signal that has become weak or distorted over a long cable, regenerates (amplifies and cleans) it and sends it on, so that the signal can travel a longer distance.

**(ii) Bridge (2 marks).** It connects two LANs or two segments of a network. It reads the hardware (MAC) address of each frame and lets through only the frames meant for the other side, which reduces unnecessary traffic.

**(iii) Router (2 marks).** It connects different networks (for example a LAN and the Internet) and forwards data packets between them, choosing the best path from the destination IP address.

**(iv) Modem (2 marks).** It *modulates* the digital signals of a computer into analogue signals that can travel over a telephone or cable line, and *demodulates* the incoming analogue signals back into digital data; it connects a computer to the Internet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Convert the following numbers to the indicated bases showing clearly the steps involved:

(i) $FD_{16}$ to binary. (3 marks)

(ii) $305_8$ to hexadecimal. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) $FD_{16}$ to binary (3 marks).** Each hexadecimal digit is replaced by its 4-bit binary equivalent:

- $F_{16} = 15_{10} = 1111_2$
- $D_{16} = 13_{10} = 1101_2$

Joining the groups: $FD_{16} = 1111\,1101_2$.

*Check:* $15 \times 16 + 13 = 253$ and $11111101_2 = 128+64+32+16+8+4+1 = 253$.

**(ii) $305_8$ to hexadecimal (3 marks).** Go through binary. Each octal digit gives 3 bits:

- $3_8 = 011_2$, $0_8 = 000_2$, $5_8 = 101_2$

So $305_8 = 011\,000\,101_2 = 011000101_2$. Regroup in fours starting from the right: $0\,|\,1100\,|\,0101$.

- $0000_2 = 0$, $1100_2 = C$, $0101_2 = 5$

Therefore $305_8 = C5_{16}$.

*Check:* $3 \times 64 + 0 \times 8 + 5 = 197$ and $C5_{16} = 12 \times 16 + 5 = 197$.

**Answers: (i) $11111101_2$; (ii) $C5_{16}$.** (Checked by a script.)
